Slice: Record Overdue Notice Failure

Intent

Record that an overdue notice could not be delivered to the borrower, so the shed manager knows the neighbor wasn't told and can follow up in person, and the borrower's My Loans shows that the notice didn't reach them.

Trigger & Actor

Externally triggered. The email provider, outside the shed, sends a final failure report for an overdue notice the shed handed it. The Email Provider Failure Report translation turns that report into the Record Overdue Notice Failure command. No person records a failure, and there is no screen.

What the report carries: the reference the shed gave the notice when it handed it over, which is the loan's ID, since each loan gets at most one overdue notice; and the reason, refused or bounced. Anything else in the report, such as the email address, is not recorded.

Command / Input

Command: Record Overdue Notice Failure

A LoanId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
loanId LoanId yes The reference from the provider's report: the loan the notice was about. Must match an Overdue Notice Sent (INV-ONF-7), for a loan that hasn't ended (INV-ONF-8).
reason Text yes refused or bounced, from the report (INV-ONF-3). Any other value is bad input.

Trigger

Triggered by: translation Email Provider Failure Report, also in this slice (externally triggered by the email provider's final failure report).

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Overdue Notice Failed → context Loans Read by: My Loans (the loan shows the notice couldn't be delivered) and Undelivered Notices (the shed manager's follow-up list).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command.
reason Text yes From the command: refused or bounced.
failedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the failure date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

The event never changes. No later event retries the notice or clears the failure.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Overdue Notice Failed feeds two views, each specified in its own doc:

  • My Loans (slices/my-loans.md) shows the borrower that the overdue notice couldn't be delivered.
  • Undelivered Notices (slices/undelivered-notices.md) lists the failure for the shed manager to follow up.

Both are eventually consistent. Overdue Loans To Notify doesn't hear this event: the loan left that list when Overdue Notice Sent was recorded.

Invariants / Business Rules

Every recorded failure is shown to the shed manager on Undelivered Notices, and to the borrower on My Loans; those views own how it is shown.

A failure is recorded only from the email provider's report; no person records it, and the only way in is the translation in Trigger & Actor. The shed records only the provider's one final failure report: the provider makes 3 delivery attempts over about an hour and reports a final failure only if all of them fail. The shed does no retrying of its own, and a failure a later attempt recovers from is never reported. How the provider's link to the shed is secured is part of the email port contract proposed for the constitution (brief 10, A5).

  • INV-ONF-3: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for the loan the notice was about, with the moment of the failure and whether the email was refused or bounced.
    • Refused and bounced are the two reasons the provider's final report can give.
  • INV-ONF-4: Every Overdue Notice Failed follows an Overdue Notice Sent for the same loan.
    • Overdue Notice Sent is recorded at hand-off, so the loan has already left Overdue Loans To Notify. Recording the failure doesn't change that list.
  • INV-ONF-6: A loan has at most one Overdue Notice Failed. No further notice is attempted for it after a failure.
    • The shed manager follows up in person.
  • INV-ONF-7: A failure report that matches no overdue notice the shed sent is ignored, and nothing is recorded.
  • INV-ONF-8: A failure report that arrives after the loan has ended, because the tool was returned or recorded lost, is ignored, and nothing is recorded.
    • For example, the borrower returned the tool during the hour the provider spent retrying.
  • INV-ONF-9: A failure report repeated for a loan whose failure is already recorded, with the same reason, succeeds and records nothing new. With a different reason it is ignored, and nothing is recorded.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Refused (INV-ONF-3)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for Ana's drill loan L1, and the drill is still out
    • When: the provider's final report says the notice for L1 was refused
    • Then: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1, reason refused, with the time it was recorded. No further notice is sent for L1.
  • Bounced (INV-ONF-3)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and the drill is still out
    • When: the provider's final report says the notice for L1 bounced
    • Then: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1, reason bounced.
  • Report matching no notice (INV-ONF-4, INV-ONF-7)
    • Given: no Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for loan L2
    • When: a failure report names L2
    • Then: ignored with no-matching-notice. Nothing is recorded.
  • Report arrives after the tool was returned (INV-ONF-8)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and Tool Returned was then recorded for L1 while the provider was still retrying
    • When: the provider's final report says the notice for L1 bounced
    • Then: ignored with loan-ended. Nothing is recorded.
  • Report arrives after the tool was recorded lost (INV-ONF-8)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and Tool Lost was then recorded for L1
    • When: the provider's final report says the notice for L1 was refused
    • Then: ignored with loan-ended. Nothing is recorded.
  • The same report arrives twice (INV-ONF-6, INV-ONF-9)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Failed was recorded for L1, reason bounced
    • When: the same report, L1 bounced, arrives again
    • Then: it succeeds and nothing new is recorded. L1 still has one Overdue Notice Failed.
  • A second report with a different reason (INV-ONF-6, INV-ONF-9)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Failed was recorded for L1, reason bounced
    • When: a report arrives saying the notice for L1 was refused
    • Then: ignored with failure-already-recorded. Nothing is recorded; L1 keeps its one failure, reason bounced.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: a stable name and a sentence. No person sees these; they go back to the translation, which takes no further action, and are kept for diagnosing the provider link.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. no-matching-notice (INV-ONF-7).
  2. A failure already recorded for the loan (INV-ONF-9): a repeat with the same reason succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise failure-already-recorded.
  3. loan-ended (INV-ONF-8).
Reason Sentence Rule
no-matching-notice No overdue notice was sent for that loan. INV-ONF-7
failure-already-recorded A failure is already recorded for that notice. INV-ONF-9
loan-ended That loan has already ended. INV-ONF-8

A missing or malformed loan ID, or a reason other than refused or bounced, is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: the provider may deliver the same final report more than once. A repeat with the same loan and reason succeeds and records nothing new, even if the loan has since ended. So one failure never shows twice on Undelivered Notices.

Retries and compensations: none in the shed. The provider's own 3 attempts happen before its final report. After a failure no further notice is attempted; following up is the shed manager's job, in person.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the email provider's failure report can trigger this command, through the translation. How the shed checks a report really comes from its provider is part of the email port contract proposed for the constitution (brief 10, A5).
  • PII & compliance: Overdue Notice Failed holds no name or email: only the loan, the reason and the time. The address the notice went to is already on Overdue Notice Sent (sentTo), so the email address in the provider's report is not recorded again.
  • Performance / SLA: none. A failure shows on Undelivered Notices shortly after the report arrives, about an hour after the notice was handed over.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice): loanId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Overdue Notice Failed (this slice): loanId, reason.
    • Overdue Notice Sent, and the loan's ID as the reference the provider quotes back, match slices/send-overdue-notice.md. Return Tool and Record Tool Lost are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Loans and Undelivered Notices (the failure).

Open Questions

None.
